verification_summary:
Adversarial verification of the four research angles. Sources were web pages, extracted PDF text, and my own scripts. The scripts read the cut data file only (D:/nt/nt_recut_data/Bitcoin_BTCUSDT_cut.csv, which ends 2025-07-20), and LOG.md was read only. Scripts: C:/Users/Step/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/d--nt-neural-trade/19204bbf-66e0-4407-bdcf-53181c7d4fa1/scratchpad/adv_verify.py, adv_verify2.py and adv_verify3.py. Extracted paper texts are in the same folder: denicola.txt, qh.txt, jaq.txt and hl.txt.

Main results:

(1) The data-provenance finding is confirmed, by an independent and decisive check. The long file is Bitstamp BTC/USD. Its timestamps are UTC+4 during US daylight saving time and UTC+5 otherwise, until a splice on 2024-09-13 08:00. Integer closes start inside file hour 12 on 2022-08-10. With the +4 h shift, that hour is 08:00-09:00 UTC, which is 10:00-11:00 Luxembourg time: exactly the window Bitstamp announced for its 0.01 to 1 tick change. Seventeen Binance windows give best lags of 300 / 240 / 0 minutes, as claimed. The DST seams, which the events angle did not inspect, are real artefacts. The spring seam drops one real hour, with a 109 bps one-minute jump on 2018-03-11. The autumn seam carries a misaligned hour.

(2) The core mechanism is confirmed. The 2017-20 one-minute reversal sits in the gap from close_t to open_{t+1}. Correlations of r_t with three targets, for 2017H2-20 / 2021-23 / 2024-25: next close-to-close return -0.079 / -0.003 / -0.011; the next gap -0.229 / -0.104 / -0.052; the next open-to-close return +0.038 / +0.041 / +0.009. The reversal is concentrated in thin bars: the slope is -0.24 in the lowest relative-volume quintile and -0.02 in the highest. The pooled Roll spread was 6-10 bps in 2017-20. This is a bid-ask bounce or stale-close signature. The mechanism angle's premise is wrong: it assumed Binance with a one-tick spread, said Roll bounce was too small, and proposed sub-minute transient impact instead. All of that is refuted.

(3) Corrections:
- "About half the 2018-20 edge disappears at next open" is about one third in AUC terms (excess over 0.5 falls from 0.095 to 0.065) and in top-10% hit rate. It is "half" only for H48's bps per trade.
- The univariate AUC of 0.38-0.42 that rises to 0.505 is for the one-minute-ahead cell. For 10-15 minute targets it is 0.434-0.464, rising to 0.498.
- "Reversal is not stronger after large moves" is wrong. The reversal is absent for small moves, grows for moderate and large ones, and only stops growing at the largest. De Nicola's one-minute table shows the same.
- The midrange null is not Working's 0.25. For Brownian motion it is 0.17-0.31, depending on the number of trades per bar.
- The residual next-open edge is not only multi-bar. The 1-bar return itself still gives a univariate AUC of 0.476-0.490 at 10-15 minutes in 2018-20.
- Bitstamp changed its matching engine once, live 2020-09-10, not twice.
- Chu-Zhang-Chan found news and event types may NOT be significant for efficiency. The crypto angle said efficiency coincides with news and events.
- In the Kim-Hansen paper, the reversal over the first half hour belongs to quarter-hour order imbalance. It is not "opening returns reverse over 30 s to 15 min".
- Tang et al. report H 0.415 rising to 0.478 in the paper body; the abstract rounds this to about 0.42 and 0.49. Their period split is the authors' choice, not an estimated break.
- The 2024-09 AUC break coincides with the splice only within H72's coarse dating. It is confounded, but it is not shown to be an artefact.

(4) New confound (inference): H72's step in HAR Spearman in 2022-10 follows Bitstamp's $1 tick. After the change, zero-return minutes in the file rose from 3-4% to 12% (Oct 2022) and 31% (Dec 2022). So the "rise" in volatility predictability is partly confounded. The level itself holds on Binance: H83 measures Spearman 0.448 on 2025-26 Binance data.

(5) The relative tick-size hypothesis is refuted as the driver. The tick was $0.01 (a relative tick of about 1e-6) while the reversal was strong. The reversal was already gone when the $1 tick arrived.

(6) Most citations are confirmed. These checked exactly, with numbers where given: Hendershott-Menkveld, Nagel, Bianchi et al., Chordia et al. 2005/2008, De Nicola (Table 3), Jaquart et al. (every accuracy), Sensoy, Takaishi-Adachi, Zargar-Kumar, Catania-Sandholdt, Aslan-Sensoy, Shen-Urquhart-Wang, Borgards, Miralles-Quirós, Urquhart 2017, Brauneis 2018/2021, Ardia et al. 2024, Dimpfl, the Bitstamp blog, the Binance zero-fee dates, the Binance futures tick change, and the Robinhood-Bitstamp close.

Unverifiable:
- Hansen-Lunde's statement that "noise fell over time" is not in the abstract or the working paper.
- Wen et al.'s content is paywalled.
- The roughly 90% fall in Binance BTC volume after the zero-fee period ended.
- The CCData and FOW derivative shares.
refuted: MECHANISM: Binance BTC/USDT spread is about one tick, so Roll bounce is too small to explain the 0.03 AUC lost to next-open; sub-minute transient impact after bursts of aggressive orders is more likely
Relative tick size (1/price) drives the reversal
